findings.name: three.js (r186 / npm 0.186.1)
findings.what_it_does: Core WebGL/WebGPU 3D engine. r186 adds SunLight (WebGPU), TSL SSAO/GTAO/OIT nodes and Gaussian splats; WebGPURenderer can force a WebGL2 backend (read in source). Hub for R3F, That Open and the Rhino 3dm loader.
findings.how_we_use_it: Pin 0.186.x with WebGLRenderer behind one renderer adapter; stock materials. Built-in loaders (OBJ, glTF, 3DM), GLTFExporter, clipping planes. Clay light from procedural RoomEnvironment via PMREMGenerator plus scene.environmentIntensity, no runtime HDRI. Fit near/far per frame; spike reversedDepthBuffer. WebGPU/TSL spike after 10 Dec.
findings.saves: Biggest ecosystem; Claude knows its API well (expected, not measured), so fewer tokens on docs and fixes.
findings.risks: Releases deprecate APIs (r186 removed PCFSoftShadowMap); WebGPU path maturing; float32 needs a local origin; reversedDepthBuffer is init-time, needs EXT_clip_control (Firefox about 2% per third-party stats) and excludes logarithmic depth.

findings.name: react-three-fiber (R3F) v9.8.2
findings.what_it_does: React renderer for three.js; v9 targets React 19. v10 alpha (alpha.6, 2026-10-17) makes WebGPU default. In 9.8.2, shadows={true} sets PCFSoftShadowMap, which r186 replaces with PCFShadowMap plus a console warning (read in source).
findings.how_we_use_it: Pin R3F 9.8.x with react 19.3.x. frameloop=demand, shadows=percentage (explicit PCFShadowMap), Canvas flat (default is ACESFilmic; composer tone-maps). performance.regress with drei AdaptiveDpr during interaction; calibrate the quality tier once at startup. Cache node thumbnails as images, not live Views. No v10 alpha.
findings.saves: Declarative scene code is shorter for Claude to write and review; drei supplies most helpers.
findings.risks: Peer range react >=19 <19.4 limits upgrades; shadows=true or soft triggers the removed PCFSoft mode; v10 changes renderer defaults and GLSL libraries need a legacy path; some add-ons stale (@react-three/a11y, 2022).

findings.name: @react-three/drei 10.7.9
findings.what_it_does: Helper library for R3F: Edges (EdgesGeometry, one Line2 per mesh), Outlines (inverted hull), Line, CameraControls, PerformanceMonitor, AdaptiveDpr, Bvh, Html, Grid, Sky, Environment, AccumulativeShadows, SoftShadows, View (multi-viewport in one Canvas).
findings.how_we_use_it: Viewport toolbox. Edges only for small imports; massing uses worker line segments. Outlines (inverted hull, supports clippingPlanes) for hover and the silhouette baseline. Environment only from local files or a PMREM map, never presets. CameraControls, AdaptiveDpr, Html labels. PerformanceMonitor for calibration or tours; no Views.
findings.saves: Replaces weeks of custom helpers; documented components keep prompts short.
findings.risks: PerformanceMonitor samples only rendered frames, so idle gaps under demand read as low fps; Edges is per-mesh main thread; View bypasses EffectComposer; Environment presets load from a third-party CDN (docs: not for production); Outlines clones geometry per mesh.

findings.name: pmndrs/postprocessing 6.39.5 + @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1
findings.what_it_does: WebGL post-processing: Outline, SSAO, SMAA, depth, tone mapping (modes include AGX and NEUTRAL, source read). @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1 depends on n8ao ^2.0.0, exports N8AO plus Kuwahara, Halftone, Linocut and Ramp for diagrammatic looks.
findings.how_we_use_it: Inside EffectComposer: N8AO (halfRes), SMAA, selection Outline, ToneMapping last (NEUTRAL or AGX; README says keep renderer tone mapping off). multiplisampling is wrong; set multisampling={0}: wrapper default is 4 and N8AO says hardware antialiasing fails with AO. Halftone and Kuwahara only in board-diagram presets.
findings.saves: Ready-made effects, including AO, instead of hand-written shaders or wrappers.
findings.risks: Peer three <0.187 blocks upgrades; v7 still beta; GLSL passes legacy under WebGPU; HalfFloat default buffers raise capture memory; Outline's mask pass uses an override material, which skips per-material clipping planes (source read, not run).

findings.name: N8AO 2.0.1
findings.what_it_does: Ambient-occlusion pass for three.js: quality presets, optional neural denoise, halfRes (README claims 2x-4x speedup), accumulation for still cameras. README: works with logarithmic depth buffers and orthographic cameras. Ships as <N8AO /> in @react-three/postprocessing; aoRadius in world units.
findings.how_we_use_it: Default AO for the clay look: <N8AO halfRes depthAwareUpsampling /> with world-space aoRadius. Accumulate when the camera rests (invalidate() under demand loop). Set quality once at startup. Lock n8ao 2.0.1. Off in Low tier. Test with ortho sections and log depth (README says supported) in S2/S3.
findings.saves: Strong depth cues for the cost of one pass, no custom AO or wrapper code.
findings.risks: WebGL only; hardware MSAA does not work with AO, use SMAA; README and GitHub say CC0-1.0 but npm lists ISC; one maintainer, 503 stars; speedup figures are vendor claims; README documents no fixed noise seed for tiled captures.
findings.license: CC0-1.0 per README and GitHub (npm: ISC)

findings.name: three-mesh-bvh 0.9.16
findings.what_it_does: Bounding-volume hierarchy for fast raycasts and spatial queries on three.js meshes; async/worker builds, BatchedMesh support, GPU SDF and path-tracing examples. Foundation for three-edge-projection and three-bvh-csg.
findings.how_we_use_it: Fast picking on large context meshes and imported BIM, built only over the analysis domain. Cast rays from grid points toward the sun for solar-access and shadow-hour modules without a GPU readback.
findings.saves: Avoids writing spatial indexing; one dependency covers picking and analysis.
findings.risks: README performance claim (500 rays on 80k polygons at 60 fps) is untested on student laptops; BVH build time and memory on huge context or IFC models; essentially one maintainer; 86 open issues+PRs.

findings.name: Manifold (manifold-3d 3.5.4)
findings.what_it_does: Guaranteed-manifold mesh boolean library in WASM. d.ts confirms twist/scale extrude, slice(height) on the X-Y plane (Z-up), volume, project, splitByPlane, hull, offset, originalID/faceID tracking and an ExecutionContext (cancel, progress).
findings.how_we_use_it: Worker massing kernel in Z-up metres: floorplate stacks, podium and tower unions, site cuts, per-floor gross area via slice() at mid-storey, sections via splitByPlane. reserveIDs per program volume so tags survive booleans (add test). Progress and cancel via withContext plus status().
findings.saves: One robust kernel for massing, areas, sections and tag tracking; avoids heavy B-rep WASM (about 2.8 MB unpacked package).
findings.risks: Triangle meshes only; JS Mesh is Float32, so local coordinates; inputs must be manifold; 3.5.4 declares esbuild-wasm and gltf-transform as non-optional peers plus runtime dependencies (install footprint, bundle size unchecked); manual delete(); STL export discouraged.
findings.popularity: 2.4k stars, 272 forks; used by OpenSCAD, Blender, Godot, Babylon.js per README

findings.name: rhino3dm.js 8.35.0 + three Rhino3dmLoader
findings.what_it_does: openNURBS compiled to WASM: read/write .3dm, geometry containers, Rhino Compute client. three.js Rhino3dmLoader decodes in workers, meshes SubD, converts Breps from stored per-face meshes and exposes layers, views, groups and file settings in userData.
findings.how_we_use_it: Import .3dm via Rhino3dmLoader with wasm hosted locally (setLibraryPath; docs example uses a CDN). Read userData.settings: modelUnitSystem, modelBasePoint, earthAnchorPoint (lat/long, modelNorth, modelEast per typings) to normalise units, position and true north; loader does not rotate Z-up. Map layers to program tags.
findings.saves: Direct Rhino import with no server; avoids a custom parser.
findings.risks: No booleans or meshing in JS (advanced ops need Rhino Compute); Breps without stored face meshes are skipped with a warning (source read, not run); loader pins 8.32.1 while npm is 8.35.0; unit, north and anchor fields not yet tested on team files.

findings.name: web-ifc 0.0.78
findings.what_it_does: C++ IFC reader/writer in WASM, multithreaded. Typings (read) define IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3, IfcMapConversion (IFC4X3 adds a Scaled variant), nullable context TrueNorth, GetModelSchema, GetCoordinationMatrix, COORDINATE_TO_ORIGIN; low-level writer. Same engine under That Open.
findings.how_we_use_it: Import in a worker, COORDINATE_TO_ORIGIN off. Read coordination matrix, IfcMapConversion (XAxisAbscissa/Ordinate give grid north), context TrueNorth and unit scaling; place models in float64 against the site origin. Write-back is v1 (spike vs ifc-lite, IfcOpenShell); 13 Nov exports glTF and .3dm.
findings.saves: Replaces a custom IFC parser; same engine that That Open and many viewers use.
findings.risks: MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft); pre-1.0; writer is entity-level (project, storeys, psets built by hand); no unit-query API in typings; Revit IFC MapConversion scale issue reported; schema typings read, not run; 79 open issues+PRs.

findings.name: ifc-lite (LTplus-AG/ifc-lite; @ifc-lite/wasm 10.4.0, parser 9.5.1, export 4.11.0)

findings.how_we_use_it: Benchmark beside web-ifc on one real Revit IFC (load time, fidelity, IFC4X3, storey and space export) before choosing the v1 importer. Check @ifc-lite/create for authoring storeys and spaces. Use only behind an importer interface.
findings.saves: Could answer schema coverage and IFC write-back questions that web-ifc leaves open, saving custom writer work.
findings.risks: Young (created 2026-01-10), company-run, MPL-2.0; README STEP export examples show property edits only; speed claims unverified; @ifc-lite/wasm unpacks to 10.5 MB; 432 stars; 41 open issues+PRs.

Copy Text2BIM's checker-and-repair loop. No free-form CAD in core.
findings.saves: Prevents spending build time on unreliable free-form text-to-CAD; schema-constrained JSON is cheap in tokens and needs fewer retries.
findings.risks: Evidence is single parts or one prototype, not towers; paper numbers not reproduced; Claude schemas reject recursion and numeric/array bounds (400 error) while OpenAI allows them, so our validator owns bounds; HN thread (about 10 voices) says LLMs are weak at spatial reasoning.

findings.name: Silhouette linework: three LDraw conditional-line materials and drei Outlines
findings.what_it_does: Conditional lines (three addons: WebGL ShaderMaterial, WebGPU NodeMaterial): a segment carries two control points and is discarded when they fall on opposite screen sides, a view-dependent silhouette test; no linewidth. drei Outlines: inverted hull with creased normals, clippingPlanes, thickness.
findings.how_we_use_it: Spike S4 on a twisted tower: the kernel worker computes control points per edge (opposite vertices of adjacent faces); compare conditional lines (1 px) with drei Outlines (screenspace, angle) for look, count and cost. Baseline is Outlines on massing only; pick one by 13 Nov. Print silhouettes stay on the vector path.
findings.saves: Avoids full-scene edge detection and custom silhouette shaders; the conditional-line shader already ships in three.
findings.risks: Conditional lines: addon, one-pixel lines (thinner at high DPR), control-point prep is ours, untested with N8AO and Outline. Outlines: hull gaps at hard creases, geometry cloned per mesh, weight not in mm.

principles.principle: Pin a WebGL2 stack now, plan WebGPU later. R3F v10 alpha is WebGPU-first, postprocessing (three <0.187) and N8AO are WebGL-only and SunLight is WebGPU-only, but three r186 WebGPURenderer can fall back to a WebGL2 backend.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Lock three 0.186.x, R3F 9.8.x, drei 10.7.x, react 19.3.x, n8ao 2.0.1 in a committed lockfile. Use stock materials and keep post effects and shader patches (CSM, SoftShadows) behind one renderer adapter. Set shadows=percentage, never true. Schedule a WebGPURenderer and TSL spike after 10 Dec.

principles.principle: Render only when something changes, and measure frame time only while frames are drawn. drei PerformanceMonitor takes timestamps from useFrame, so idle gaps under frameloop=demand count as elapsed time and read as low fps (source read). R3F documents regress() for interaction-time drops, and drei AdaptiveDpr reads it. Anatomy's WebGL rules cap DPR near 1.5 and stop idle loops.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: frameloop=demand. At startup run a 2-3 s calibration with frameloop=always (our own sampler that ignores gaps over about 100 ms, or PerformanceMonitor mounted only then) and store the tier per device in localStorage as a convenience, with a visible manual toggle. During orbit and drag use performance.regress plus AdaptiveDpr; verify that dpr changes redraw (call invalidate()). Mount PerformanceMonitor only for tours. AO and soft-shadow accumulation only at rest. Node thumbnails: render once offscreen and cache as images, because View calls gl.render directly and skips composer effects. Handle webglcontextlost and restored.

principles.principle: Keep lines thin, calm and computed once, with a separate view-dependent silhouette layer. Kernel edges (originalID/faceID boundaries plus a dihedral threshold) are static, so on twisted or tapered towers the view-dependent outline needs its own technique: three's conditional-line materials (WebGL and WebGPU variants, no linewidth) or drei Outlines (inverted hull, clippingPlanes). drei Edges builds EdgesGeometry per mesh on the main thread. Screen pixel widths are not print weights.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Viewport lines 1 to 1.5 px: silhouette darker than creases, context lighter. The kernel worker computes crease edges plus conditional-line control points and sends one merged LineSegments2 per layer; drei Edges only for small imports. Spike S4 compares conditional lines with drei Outlines (the baseline) on a twisted tower. Postprocessing Outline for multi-select only; no full-scene edge detection. Print weights are set in mm in the vector path (board principle).

principles.principle: Monochrome clay with one lit accent, every colour a token, and a fixed lighting rig. Matte white depends on image-based light and tone mapping: drei Environment presets load from a third-party CDN (docs: not for production), R3F Canvas defaults to ACESFilmic, and RoomEnvironment is procedural. Colour must not be the only signal (WCAG 1.4.1); cividis was designed for red-green colour-vision deficiency; jet-like ramps read poorly. Agent-made hero art is slow and token-hungry, so time-box it.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Token ladder plate/hi/edge/mid/lo/accent with light and dark values, plate equal to the viewport background. Rig: RoomEnvironment via PMREMGenerator with scene.environmentIntensity as a token, plus the SunCalc directional light; any HDRI self-hosted via files and path; Canvas flat with ToneMapping NEUTRAL or AGX last; golden-image test of the clay preset. Analysis ramps cividis or viridis (diverging only for signed deltas) with legend and units. FALSE ASSUMPTION gets an icon, label and hatch as well as its colour, contrast-checked in both themes and kept out of UI chrome. Hero figures capped, cached, never regenerated per user.

principles.principle: Interaction respects attention and access. Anatomy motion.md: parts follow targets with springs or exponential easing, the loop sleeps when idle or offscreen, reduced motion jumps to end state, the selected assembly is the single lit accent. A forum thread (4 voices, none disputing) backs a semantic DOM mirror, keyboard use and live regions; @react-three/a11y is stale.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Apply to explode sliders, camera bookmarks and node hover; cap frame dt at 1/30 s. Hit areas that stay still, short tweens for discrete picks, a designed rest pose and clamped reach appear in neither Hairline nor Anatomy: record as team assumptions. Mirror node list and metrics in a hidden HTML layer with live regions; full keyboard navigation; no autoplay beyond user-started tours.

principles.principle: Section cuts are a stencil-plus-clipping recipe; plan, section and axon drawing geometry should come from the mesh kernel and three-edge-projection, not the render pass. In r186 an override material replaces the mesh material in a pass, so per-material clipping planes do not carry over (source read). three-edge-projection projects along Y only and its SilhouetteGenerator is top-down with no view parameter; OrthographicCamera cannot shear.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Viewport sections: clipping planes plus stencil caps on watertight meshes; test EffectComposer stencilBuffer, N8AO and Outline together, fall back to renderer-level clippingPlanes if Outline leaks. Board drawings: Manifold slice() polygons to SVG for poche and plans; three-edge-projection for hidden-line roof and plan views; section lines via PlanarIntersectionGenerator or slice. Axon presets: isometric, dimetric, military plan-oblique (plan true, per Wikipedia's definition); oblique views need a shear in the projection matrix (viewport) and the same shear baked into geometry before projection (print); 30/60 variant is a team assumption; test N8AO with the sheared matrix.

principles.principle: Towers need a mesh kernel in a worker. Massing needs extrude, twist, taper, booleans, area and volume; B-rep WASM is large (replicad build about 23 MB, opencascade.js about 9 MB, occt-wasm about 4.5 MB brotli) and mainly serves detail parts. Heavy kernels and parsers belong in workers with manual memory care: Rhino3dmLoader decodes in workers, occt-wasm requires release(), Manifold objects need delete(), and ExecutionContext cancels only once an eager call such as status() runs.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: One kernel worker pool with a typed message API; massing nodes run on Manifold and report volume, gross floorplate area per floor (slice at mid-storey, since slice at the bottom returns base faces and at the top returns empty) and surface area. FSR exclusions belong to the policy module. Each node result carries a dispose hook; progress and cancel via withContext plus status(); for slider drags debounce and terminate the worker. Replicad or occt-wasm only as optional v1 detail modules loaded on demand.

principles.principle: AI geometry generation is unreliable for free-form CAD and is trained on mechanical parts. Reported figures: 69.3% exact match for a fine-tuned model on single parts, +5% from visual feedback, no Zoo benchmarks. Text2BIM uses a rule-checker repair loop. A Hacker News thread (about 10 voices) says LLMs are weak at spatial reasoning. Structured-output limits differ: Claude rejects recursion, numeric bounds and array bounds beyond minItems 0 or 1, and caps optional parameters at 24 and anyOf or type-array parameters at 16; OpenAI strict mode allows recursion and bounds, up to 10 nesting levels and 5,000 properties.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Text-to-massing: the LLM returns a flat JSON node list (enum node types, id references, params as name/value pairs, all fields required) that passes both providers' schema rules; test the one schema against both APIs. Our validator checks positive volume, manifoldness, bounds and graph acyclicity with Manifold, then we render and let the user edit. Log every AI output as an editable team assumption.

principles.principle: Licence hygiene decides what ships. AGPL (xeokit, Theatre Studio) and LGPL WASM (OCCT builds) carry obligations; MPL-2.0 (web-ifc, ifc-lite) is file-level; Zlib, MIT, Apache-2.0 and CC0 are easy. N8AO is CC0 on GitHub but ISC on npm. Third-party tile services add terms (Google Map Tiles policy); so do AI image services and the competition's own terms.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Decide the platform's own licence first (open question for the team). Keep a THIRD_PARTY licence table in the repo; ship LGPL WASM with source and relink notice; never bundle AGPL code unless the platform is AGPL; record service terms for any streamed tiles and any AI image model before they reach a board.

principles.principle: Prefer in-browser WASM over native Python on student Windows machines, and fix the runtime once. Smart App Control can block unsigned OCP, CadQuery pip supports Python 3.9-3.12, and Node is not yet installed. Node 24 entered Maintenance on 2026-10-20 (supported to 2028-04-30); 22 ends 2027-04-30; 26 becomes LTS on 2026-10-28; Vite 8.3.5 needs Node ^20.19 or >=22.12.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Core runs in the browser with no native installs beyond Node 24.22.x, pinned in .nvmrc and package.json engines (do not start on 22). Any Python CAD stays optional: OCP.wasm in the browser or a documented WSL/conda path, with telemetry opt-out.

principles.principle: One canonical project frame, converted at the boundaries, including true north. Manifold slices on X-Y (Z-up) and its JS Mesh is Float32; Rhino and IFC are Z-up; glTF is Y-up in metres; OBJ has no unit field. Downtown Vancouver's street grid runs about 45 degrees off true north (our calculation from City public-streets segments: Georgia, Dunsmuir, Robson near 134.6 deg; Hornby, Burrard, Granville, Howe, Seymour near 44.8 deg), so grid-aligned models carry a large rotation. Rhino stores modelNorth, IFC stores context TrueNorth plus grid north in IfcMapConversion (IfcOpenShell convention); OBJ and glTF carry none. UTM 10 convergence downtown is about -0.09 deg (our calculation). LiDAR 2022 is UTM 10 NAD83(CSRS), near 5.46 million m northing, where float32 steps 0.5 m.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Project file stores metres, Z-up, site origin (block centroid), CRS (EPSG:3157 or 26910, confirmed per dataset), vertical datum and northAngle (degrees, anticlockwise from project +Y to true north). Importers convert in float64 (proj4js): Rhino modelUnitSystem, modelBasePoint, earthAnchorPoint and modelNorth; IFC unit scaling, GetCoordinationMatrix, IfcMapConversion and TrueNorth (null means unknown, not 0); OBJ asks for units; glTF metres Y-up. OBJ, glTF and SKP imports prompt for north with a visible arrow and a snap-to-street-grid helper; the sun and shadow module blocks until north is confirmed. Tests: a 10 m cube in mm .3dm, m .ifc and OBJ gives 1000 m3 and 100 m2 per slice; a box rotated 30 deg in its source file gives the same shadow polygon after import; two IFCs from one Revit model overlay within 1 mm; a tile round-trips within 1 mm.

principles.principle: Size the world from the sun, not from the model, and shadows fan out. At 49.28 N on 21 Dec the solar-time noon sun is about 17.3 deg (geometric): a 305 m tower casts about 980 m at noon, 1.4 km at 10:00 and 2.5 km at 09:00, whose tip lies about 1.6 km west and 1.9 km north of the base (our calculation); equinox noon about 355 m. SunCalc altitude is apparent (refraction-corrected): 0.05 to 0.13 deg higher, shadows 0.3% to 1.8% shorter. 10:00 PST is about 09:49 solar (longitude and equation of time).
principles.rule_for_our_tool: The analysis window is an editable team assumption. Domain = the footprint swept along each analysed shadow vector (a fan polygon) plus margin: about 3.3 km east-west by 1.9 km deep for 09:00-15:00 solar on 21 Dec, about 1.3 by 1.2 km for 10:00-14:00. Set context scope, shadow-camera fit (and CSM maxFar), BVH extent and analysis grid from it; coarse LOD far out. Use SunCalc with real timestamps; document apparent vs geometric altitude and test against JPL Horizons apparent values. Fit near/far per frame; S3 compares reversedDepthBuffer, logarithmic depth (N8AO supports it) and near/far fit with caps and Outline.

principles.principle: Boards are a JPEG deliverable built by a capture pipeline, not a screenshot. Terms: each panel a JPEG of at most 10 MB, up to four, anonymous, portal upload; pixel size is not in the terms (brief). A2 at 300 dpi is 4961 x 7016 px (34.8 Mpx, 139 MB per RGBA8 buffer), giving about 2.3 bits per pixel at 10 MB; at 150 dpi (2480 x 3508, 8.7 Mpx) about 9 (our arithmetic). setViewOffset tiles seam under N8AO, SMAA and Outline unless padded. JPEG artefacts hit hairlines first; canvas.toBlob JPEG exposes quality only and writes 96 dpi metadata; @jsquash/jpeg (mozjpeg WASM) exposes chroma_subsample but takes one full ImageData.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Tiles with a gutter (start 128 px) are cropped and stitched in a worker; vector overlay (Manifold slices, three-edge-projection) is composited with weights in mm (starting 0.13, 0.18, 0.35, 0.5 mm; ISO 128-2:2020 via a secondary source; team assumption); sRGB JPEG size-search under a margin below 10 MB; strip metadata; check anonymity (no names, logos, platform branding) and do not publish board visuals before submission (Terms 4.1). Choose dpi from the brief and the size test (150 to 300), not from A2 alone. PDF (svg2pdf.js, jsPDF) only for the course. Tests: 2x2 tiled vs single render; dense-linework ringing on 0.13 mm lines; weakest laptop.

principles.principle: AI rendering is a styled image made from a reference render, not a geometry-locked pass. The OpenAI guide documents reference images and prompt-based masks (applied to the first image) but no depth, normal or ControlNet input; edge at most 3840 px, 0.66 to 8.29 Mpx, above 2560x1440 experimental, layout control weak. At 300 dpi 3840 px is about 325 mm and 2560 px about 217 mm; a full A2 portrait image tops out near 146 dpi (2416 x 3424; our arithmetic). Buildner advises checking AI-tool terms.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Send a clay+AO+hairline beauty render as the reference image (gpt-image-2.5-sunburst for edit precision); no depth or normals to OpenAI. Place AI images within their native size or upscale and label; composite vector linework over them so geometry stays authoritative; run a silhouette-IoU check against the clay render (threshold a team assumption); record model, date and prompt. Open-weights depth route for geometric lock (SDXL depth ControlNet, openrail++; FLUX.1 Depth dev, non-commercial licence, gated, GPU) is roadmap and untested.

recommendations.decision: Adopt Vite 8.3 + React 19.3 + TypeScript + three 0.186.1 + R3F 9.8.2 + drei 10.7.9 on the WebGL2 renderer, pinned in a committed lockfile (npm, npm ci), with Canvas shadows=percentage and flat (tone mapping from the composer). Install Node 24.22.x now and pin it in .nvmrc and engines; lock n8ao 2.0.1. Keep COMPAT and THIRD_PARTY files (three below 0.187, react below 19.4, monthly upgrade check, licence table, AGPL blocked in CI, LGPL WASM shipped with source notice). Accept npm's auto-install of manifold-3d's peers (esbuild-wasm, gltf-transform) and confirm in the Vite bundle report that only manifold.js and the wasm ship; add npm overrides for three-edge-projection's stale peers.
recommendations.rationale: Peer ranges line up today (R3F react >=19 <19.4, postprocessing three <0.187, That Open three >=0.182) and Vite 8.3.5 needs Node ^20.19 or >=22.12. Node 24 entered Maintenance on 2026-10-20 but is supported to 2028-04-30, while 22 ends 2027-04-30. R3F 9.8.2's default soft shadows hit a mode r186 removed, and its default ACESFilmic tone mapping would tint white clay. A small compat file prevents rework before 13 Nov.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: R3F v10 alpha/WebGPU-first (pre-release, N8AO and postprocessing are WebGL-only); Babylon.js (ecosystem mismatch); raw three.js without R3F; floating caret versions; Node 22; waiting for Node 26 LTS (28 Oct) before starting; a pnpm packageExtensions workaround (not tested).

recommendations.decision: Default look 'Clay and Hairline' under a fixed lighting rig: matte white massing lit by RoomEnvironment via PMREMGenerator (no runtime HDRI; any HDRI self-hosted), ToneMapping NEUTRAL or AGX last, golden-image tested; 1 to 1.5 px kernel crease edges plus a view-dependent silhouette layer (S4: conditional lines vs drei Outlines baseline); built-in <N8AO halfRes /> with multisampling 0, SMAA, hover Outlines, one accent. Presets: Section (ortho, stencil caps), Exploded axon (isometric, dimetric, military plan-oblique), Analysis (cividis or viridis, legends; FALSE ASSUMPTION marked by icon, label and hatch as well as colour), Diagram (halftone/Kuwahara). Node thumbnails rendered once and cached. Adopt Hairline tokens and its static package; Anatomy only for a few spend-capped hero figures; treat hairline, anatomy and text-to-cad as dev-time resources and confirm with Xun which repos she meant.
recommendations.rationale: Matches the instructor-shared tools' restraint and uses cheap existing components. Static kernel edges miss silhouettes on twisted towers, and drei Environment presets load from a third-party CDN (docs: not for production), so the rig is procedural and offline-safe. Colour-only flags fail WCAG 1.4.1. drei View bypasses the composer (source read), so thumbnails are cached images.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Photoreal PBR as default (heavy on laptops, distracts from analysis); full-scene screen-space edge detection (extra pass, noisy); static kernel edges alone for silhouettes; drei Environment presets; rainbow ramps; colour-only FALSE ASSUMPTION marking; a custom N8AO wrapper; drei Edges for massing and context; live drei Views for node cards; per-module generated illustrations; Theatre.js for motion (stalled, AGPL studio).

recommendations.decision: Use Manifold (manifold-3d 3.5.4) in a worker as the massing and boolean kernel in Z-up metres: extrude (twist/taper), union/subtract, slice-to-area at mid-storey, volume, project and section split. Carry program tags with reserveIDs/originalID, compute feature edges in the worker and send merged line segments, cache results by parameter hash, and drive progress and cancel through ExecutionContext plus status().
recommendations.rationale: One 2.8 MB-unpacked package covers tower massing, per-floor gross area and sections; guaranteed-manifold booleans reduce debugging; tags and edges come from the same mesh output. slice() at the bottom returns base faces and at the top returns empty, so slice mid-storey and label the result 'gross floorplate area'. Replicad or occt-wasm only as optional v1 detail modules.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: opencascade.js (stale since 2023); JSCAD (BSP booleans, anecdotal speed and manifoldness problems); three-bvh-csg (experimental, needs manifold inputs); CadQuery or build123d via Pyodide in core (not in the official package list; OCP.wasm roadmap only).

recommendations.decision: Add a canonical-frame rule to the project file and every importer: metres, Z-up kernel and analysis frame, site origin at the block centroid, CRS (EPSG:3157 or 26910, confirmed per dataset), vertical datum and a northAngle (degrees, anticlockwise from project +Y to true north); float64 transforms (proj4js) at import and export; Manifold, BVH and three.js receive local coordinates only; one root transform maps to the Y-up render frame (or DEFAULT_UP Z, chosen in the spike). Read north from Rhino modelNorth, IFC TrueNorth and IfcMapConversion; prompt for it on OBJ, glTF and SKP imports with a north arrow and a snap-to-street-grid helper (about 44.8 and 134.6 deg downtown); the sun module blocks until north is confirmed. Tests: 10 m cube in mm .3dm, m .ifc and OBJ gives 1000 m3 and 100 m2 per slice; a box rotated 30 deg in its source gives the same shadow polygon; two IFCs from one Revit model overlay within 1 mm; a tile round-trips within 1 mm.
recommendations.rationale: Mixed units, axes and north fail silently: mm read as metres is a 1e6 area error, a Z/Y mix-up slices the tower sideways, and a 45 deg north error (the downtown grid angle, our calculation) swings every shadow, 1 deg moving a 2.49 km shadow tip about 43 m. Vancouver LiDAR is UTM 10 near 5.46 million m northing, where float32 steps 0.5 m; Manifold's JS Mesh is Float32, so the fix precedes the kernel.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Rendering in raw UTM coordinates; relying on float64 inside the Manifold kernel (JS API is Float32); xeokit double-precision viewer (AGPL, separate renderer); letting each importer pick its own frame; assuming project +Y is true north; web-ifc COORDINATE_TO_ORIGIN per file (misaligns multi-file projects).

recommendations.decision: Importers and context for 13 Nov: first download the Challenge brief with its site plans and 3D model (email-gated; registration closes 29 Oct, Q&A 3 Nov) and import that model as the default context, recording format, units, CRS and LOD. Then .3dm via Rhino3dmLoader with local rhino3dm wasm, IFC read via web-ifc 0.0.78 in a worker, OBJ/glTF via three loaders; export glTF (GLTFExporter) and .3dm. City LiDAR 2022 (buildings class), preprocessed offline into compact glTF, only fills gaps or extends the sun-fan domain beyond the supplied model; footprints 2015 for comparison only. v1: 3d-tiles-renderer for optional visual context after a Google and Cesium terms check; spikes: web-ifc vs ifc-lite vs IfcOpenShell on a real Revit IFC, That Open Fragments in R3F vs a lazy BIM inspector.
recommendations.rationale: The brief page lists site plans and a 3D model, so a LiDAR conversion is not the default path. All importers run client-side with no server cost. LiDAR tiles are 16 MB to 2.74 GB zipped, too large for the browser; footprints are 2015, approximate, without heights. Google tiles bar offline use, analysis and tracing 3D objects, so they suit live visuals only. IFC write-back with web-ifc is entity-level, so it moves to v1.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: xeokit (AGPL-3.0); Speckle viewer as the viewport (Viewer 2 cannot render current bundles); Google tiles as analysis geometry (terms); loading raw LAS in the browser; LiDAR as the default context while the official model exists; promising IFC export for 13 Nov; mixing That Open's renderer beside R3F untested.

recommendations.decision: Implement text-to-massing, not free-form text-to-CAD: the LLM returns a flat JSON node list (enum node types, id references, params as name/value pairs, no recursion, no numeric bounds) through structured outputs; Manifold validates (volume, manifoldness, bounds, acyclic graph), we render and check, and the user edits parameters. Follow Text2BIM's checker-and-repair pattern. Install earthtojake/text-to-cad only as a developer Claude Code plugin for small details; Zoo API only as an optional flagged integration later.
recommendations.rationale: Published text-to-CAD results come from single mechanical parts (69.3% exact match at best); Text2BIM is the architecture-specific precedent. Claude structured outputs reject recursive schemas, numeric and most array bounds and cap optional parameters at 24, so a nested graph schema returns 400 errors; OpenAI strict mode is looser, so one flat schema serves both and our validator owns bounds.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Free-form LLM-to-CadQuery in core; Zoo Text-to-CAD as a dependency (hosted engine, credit cost, no benchmarks); cad0 (7B-class mechanical-part model); nested or recursive graph schemas.

recommendations.decision: Sun and shadow: SunCalc 2.1.1 behind one tested wrapper (real America/Vancouver timestamps; apparent vs geometric altitude decided once and documented) drives a directional light in WebGL with shadows=percentage; drei Sky for the sky; accumulate soft ground shadows only when still. Size the analysis domain as a fan, the footprint swept along each analysed shadow vector (about 3.3 km east-west by 1.9 km deep for 09:00-15:00 solar on 21 Dec, about 1.3 by 1.2 km for 10:00-14:00; window is a team assumption). One-day spike on three 0.186.1: single light with shadow camera fitted to the domain (4096 map) vs CSM vs AccumulativeShadows; CSM only if near-camera texels look poor; drop SoftShadows from core. Shadow hours come from BVH raycasts from grid points, not rendered pixels.
recommendations.rationale: Analysis must be reproducible and citable while the visual shadow is only illustrative. Our calculation gives a 305 m tower a noon shadow of 980 m on 21 Dec and a 09:00 tip 1.6 km west and 1.9 km north, so a few-hundred-metre or north-only box silently truncates it. SunCalc altitude is refraction-corrected, which shortens shadows 0.3% to 1.8% against the geometric figures. CSM patches shaders and will not port to WebGPU; SunLight is WebGPU-documented; PCFSoftShadowMap was removed in r186.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: SunLight addon now (WebGPU only); takram atmosphere now; CSM by default; SoftShadows in core; AccumulativeShadows as the analysis source (planar ground catcher); default shadows=true; a northward box as the domain.

recommendations.decision: Board capture service (owner needed), ending in JPEG: render the raster underlay (clay, AO, shadows) in tiles with camera.setViewOffset and a gutter of at least 128 px, crop and stitch in a worker, composite the vector overlay (Manifold slices, three-edge-projection; weights in mm, 0.13/0.18/0.35/0.5 as a team assumption), convert to sRGB and encode JPEG with a size-search loop kept under 10 MB (canvas.toBlob, or @jsquash/jpeg for chroma control; margin and dpi chosen by test). Strip metadata; check that no names, logos or platform branding appear; keep board visuals unpublished until submission. PDF via svg2pdf.js and jsPDF only for the course review. Read board size and orientation from the brief. Pass a 2x2 seam test and a dense-linework JPEG test, and test on the weakest laptop before 13 Nov.
recommendations.rationale: Terms 4.8 require JPEG panels of at most 10 MB, up to four; non-compliance may disqualify. A2 at 300 dpi is 34.8 Mpx, about 2.3 bits per pixel at 10 MB (our arithmetic), so dpi may have to drop. Screen-space passes lack data beyond a tile edge, and JPEG damages 1-1.5 px hairlines first. Terms 4.1 bars previously published visuals, so public sharing of board images before 30 Nov is a risk.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: A2 300 dpi PDF as the final output; single full-size canvas capture; screenshots of the live viewport; raster linework in print; ungutted tiles; one fixed JPEG quality; pdf-lib (last release 2021).

recommendations.decision: Performance budget and measured spikes: frameloop demand; startup tier calibration with frameloop=always (own sampler or PerformanceMonitor mounted only then); interaction-time DPR via performance.regress plus AdaptiveDpr; instancing, BVH picking, N8AO half-res, cached thumbnails, Low/Medium/High tiers with a visible toggle, context-loss handling. Before 13 Nov run and log measured numbers for: S1 shadows (fitted light vs CSM), S2 section (stencil + composer + N8AO + Outline, orthographic), S3 depth (near/far fit vs reversedDepthBuffer vs logarithmic depth on a 2 km scene, with caps and Outline), S4 twisted-tower edges and silhouettes (worker edges vs drei Edges; conditional lines vs Outlines), S5 tile seams plus JPEG under 10 MB on dense linework, S6 unit, frame and north tests, S7 weakest-laptop smoke test; by 10 Dec S8 real Revit IFC importer comparison and S9 gpt-image fidelity (silhouette IoU) on clay references.
recommendations.rationale: PerformanceMonitor counts idle gaps as slow frames under frameloop=demand (source read), so the two rules conflicted. Vendor figures (N8AO 2x-4x, BVH 500 rays at 60 fps, ifc-lite 5x) are unverified and nothing was measured on a team laptop, so each spike needs a pass/fail number. 23 days remain to 13 Nov, so S1-S7 fit about 5 working days.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: PerformanceMonitor permanently mounted under a demand loop; fixed high quality for everyone; many Canvas elements or live Views for node cards; avoiding log depth on an unverified N8AO fear; WebGPU path-tracing for the live view (three-gpu-pathtracer needs WebGPU and long convergence).

recommendations.decision: AI render hand-off: send gpt-image a clay+AO+hairline beauty render as the reference image (gpt-image-2.5-sunburst for edit precision, -flare for drafts), not depth or normal passes. Request at most 2560x1440 (3840x2160 is experimental) and place the result at its native size (about 217 mm wide at 300 dpi) or upscale and label it; composite our vector linework over it; run a silhouette-IoU check against the clay render; log model name, date and prompt as an editable assumption. If geometric lock is required, record a depth-ControlNet route (SDXL depth ControlNet, openrail++; FLUX.1 Depth dev, non-commercial licence, gated) as a roadmap alternative for the presentation packet.
recommendations.rationale: The OpenAI image guide documents reference images and prompt-based masks, not depth conditioning, caps edges at 3840 px and 8.29 Mpx, and calls layout-sensitive placement difficult, so geometry can drift. Buildner advises checking AI-tool terms and not treating AI images as sole work. Keeping vector linework authoritative protects drawing accuracy on the boards.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Exporting depth, normal and line passes to gpt-image (unsupported); one AI image filling an A2 board at 300 dpi (limit near 146 dpi at best); AI image as the only board content; depth-ControlNet in core (GPU hosting, licence checks, untested).
